headline: In 1977 a telescope in Ohio picked up a 72-second signal from deep space. It has never been explained.
slides: Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope was scanning the sky for signs of intelligent life.
A powerful signal came through for exactly as long as the telescope could see that patch of sky.
That is how its strength printed out: a code for a signal far above the background noise.
Days later, astronomer Jerry Ehman found it on the printout, circled it in red pen and wrote one word.
It seemed to come from the direction of the constellation Sagittarius.
Astronomers have looked many times since. It has never been detected again.
sources: Sources: Ohio State University Big Ear Radio Observatory, Jerry R. Ehman, Discover Magazine
